items.question: How many areas does the AW189 external pre-flight check sequence cover?
items.explanation: The pre-flight check sequence covers 7 areas: nose, fuselage RH side, tail boom RH side, fin/gearboxes/tail rotor, tail boom LH side, fuselage LH side, and cabin/cockpit interior.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — External Pre-Flight Checks, Figure 2A-1

items.question: During engine pre-start checks, roughly how long does it take for the APU generator to come online after selecting START?
items.explanation: After momentarily selecting SEL MODE to START and releasing to ON, the time required for the APU GEN to come online is approximately 40–45 seconds.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Engine Pre-Start Checks (APU)

items.question: During the FIRE test in pre-start checks, what is the correct sequence of aural/visual indications?
options: APU FIRE, then Engine 1, then Engine 2, then BAG FIRE
ENGINE 1 FIRE, ENGINE 2 FIRE, APU FIRE, then BAG FIRE (WARNING WARNING)
BAG FIRE first, then engines, then APU
items.explanation: The FIRE test sequence is: audio tone/voice 'ENGINE 1 FIRE', then 'ENGINE 2 FIRE', then 'APU FIRE', and finally 'WARNING WARNING' with the BAG FIRE CAS warning.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Engine Pre-Start Checks (APU), Fire Test

items.question: At what NG value should the ENG 1 MODE switch be selected to IDLE, provided ITT is below 150°C?
items.explanation: ENG 1 MODE switch is selected to IDLE when ITT is below 150°C and NG is 0%.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Engine Starting

items.question: At what percentage does the No. 1 engine starter disengage during a normal start?
items.explanation: The engine starter disengages at 52% ±2% NG.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Engine Starting

items.question: What is the stabilized idle NF/NR speed after both engines have started?
items.explanation: With both engines at idle, NF/NR stabilizes at 73% ±1% (the single-engine idle value is 55% ±1% before the second engine is started).
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Engine Starting

items.question: After both engines are selected to FLT, what NR/NF value should be confirmed stabilized?
items.explanation: After engine 1 & 2 MODE switches are selected to FLT, confirm NR/NF stabilized at 102%.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — After Engine Start Checks

items.question: What action is taken if a failed engagement occurs during engine start, indicated by NF possibly higher than NR and near-zero torque?
options: Shut down the non-engaged engine first, then when stopped shut down the other engine
Immediately shut down both engines simultaneously
items.explanation: If a failed engagement occurs, shut down the non-engaged engine first and, once it has stopped, shut down the other engine. If a hard engagement occurs, shut down both engines for maintenance action.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — After Engine Start Checks, Caution

items.question: During the Category B Hover IGE takeoff, at what height is the hover established?
items.explanation: Category B Hover IGE takeoff establishes the hover at 7 ft AGL, respecting the controllability WAT charts for prevailing wind conditions.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Category B Take-Off (Hover IGE)

items.question: During a Category B Hover IGE takeoff, at what airspeed should the aircraft achieve 50 ft above the takeoff surface?
items.explanation: Accelerate forward and climb to achieve 50 ft (15 m) above the takeoff surface at 40 KIAS, continuing up to 80 KIAS (Vy).
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Category B Take-Off (Hover IGE)

items.question: What is Vy (best rate of climb speed) for the AW189?
items.explanation: Vy is 80 KIAS, used as the climb speed after clearing obstacles on takeoff.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Category B Take-Off

items.question: During takeoff, above what height AGL should the landing gear be selected UP?
items.explanation: Landing gear is selected UP above 200 ft (61 m) AGL. For OAT of -30°C and below, undercarriage retraction time may increase.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Category B Take-Off

items.question: In the LD SHARE function on the ECDU MISC page, what does it allow the pilot to control?
options: Engine TQ or ITT matching between the two engines
items.explanation: The LD-SHARE switch allows the pilot to maintain engine TQ or ITT matched between engines, as required.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — After Take-Off, Note

items.question: Below what height AGL should the crew 'fly attentive'?
items.explanation: During flight below 500 ft (150 m) AGL, the crew should fly attentive.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — After Take-Off

items.question: For a Category B landing, at what height and airspeed should the initial deceleration to stabilize 40 KIAS begin?
options: 200 ft above touchdown, no more than 500 fpm
items.explanation: Reduce airspeed gradually to arrive at 200 ft above the touchdown point with a rate of descent of no more than 500 fpm, initiating a deceleration to stabilize 40 KIAS at 50 ft.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Approach and Landing, Category B Landing

items.question: During a Category B landing, at 50 ft the aircraft rotates nose up to decelerate — by how many degrees?
items.explanation: At 50 ft, rotate nose up to obtain an attitude change of 5° to decelerate before descending to a hover at 7 ft AGL.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Approach and Landing, Category B Landing

items.question: When descending below 150 ft AGL Rad Alt height, what vocal message is activated regardless of landing gear status?
items.explanation: When descending below 150 ft AGL Rad Alt height, a vocal message 'ONE FIFTY FEET' is activated regardless of landing gear status; this message is suppressed if AWG is set to REGRADE.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Category B Landing, Note

items.question: During engine and rotor shutdown, what is the mandatory stabilization period at IDLE (or below 90% NG) before selecting ENG MODE switches OFF?
items.explanation: A period of 2 minutes stabilization at IDLE, or with NG less than 90%, is mandatory before setting the ENG 1 and 2 MODE switches to OFF.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Engines and Rotor Shutdown

items.question: Below what NR is the rotor brake selected to BRAKE during shutdown, and what is the recommended range?
options: Below 100% NR; any time after engine shutdown
items.explanation: Below 40% NR, select the rotor brake lever to BRAKE (recommended between 20% and 40% NR), confirming no abnormal pressure messages illuminate.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Engines and Rotor Shutdown

items.question: Why should the rotor brake be avoided on ice or another slippery/loose surface?
options: It could damage the brake pucks
It could cause the helicopter to rotate
items.explanation: Avoid use of the rotor brake if the helicopter is on ice or another slippery or loose surface, to prevent rotation of the helicopter.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Engines and Rotor Shutdown, Caution

items.question: At or below what OAT should the Main and Auxiliary batteries be removed and stored in a heated room if the helicopter remains parked outside?
items.explanation: If the helicopter is to remain parked outside with an OAT at or below -20°C, both Main and Auxiliary (if fitted) batteries should be removed and stored in a heated room.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Cold Weather Operation

items.question: During autorotative descent, what is the maximum NR permitted?
items.explanation: During autorotative descent, maximum NR is 110%; rotor speed is sensitive in low-power descent and autorotation, so care is needed to avoid exceeding limits.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Autorotative Descent

items.question: What approximate airspeed should be maintained during autorotative descent?
items.explanation: Adjust attitude to obtain approximately 80 KIAS during autorotative descent.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Autorotative Descent

items.question: To recover from autorotation to powered flight, what minimum torque should be confirmed once freewheels are joined?
items.explanation: To recover to powered flight, slowly increase collective pitch until freewheels are joined and at least 15% torque is indicated, then gently increase power over not less than 3 seconds.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Autorotative Descent

items.question: During cruise checks, what is noted about the APU EECU FAIL message on the ENGINE synoptic page?
options: It always indicates a critical APU failure requiring shutdown
It can be disregarded when not associated with an APU CAS message — the APU functions normally
It requires immediate APU shutdown and inspection
It only appears during APU start, never in cruise
items.explanation: Disregard the APU EECU FAIL message which may illuminate on the ENGINE synoptic page when not associated with an APU CAS message — the APU functions normally in that case.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 2A — Cruise Checks, Note
